answer: Street sound outside a window is a live, unrepeatable stream: passing cars, a distant siren, and a dog barking arrive in an order no script can predict, and a phone can prove its place by matching its recording against a city microphone network in the same minute. A farm in one warehouse hears only ventilation, so it cannot reproduce thirty different streets at once. A vine of traffic noise climbs and falls by the hour, a canyon of tall buildings channels the sound, and the summit of rush hour peaks at a moment only a real street can witness.
